newsitem.title: CANADA: Light rain seen for Canadian Prairies Thurs-Fri.
newsitem.headline: Light rain seen for Canadian Prairies Thurs-Fri.

text.p: Canada's Prairies were forecast to see light rains on Thursday and Friday, Environment Canada said Wednesday.

Manitoba and Saskatchewan were seen having a 30 percent probability of precipitation Thursday, while the region between Edmonton and Calgary, Alberta, faces a 50 percent chance of getting less than five mm (0.2 inch) of rain, meteorologist Karen Dewar said.
Scattered showers were forecast for the Prairie grainbelt on Friday with five mm expected to fall on Alberta's foothills and five mm around Prince Albert, Saskatchewan.
Southeast Manitoba may see the most rain Friday with up to 10 mm (0.4 inch) expected.
"The (wheat) crop's filling now, it needs moisture now, in the next week to 10 days," said Paul Bullock, Canadian Wheat Board weather and crop surveillance director.
Prairie spring wheat fields, which total 21.955 million acres, are in the heading stage now, he said.
